contracts: Domain-owning object revalidates actual credential/session identity and current permission; public DTO identity cannot override actor.
REST and IRC share durable message/channel/role operations; canonical IDs and revisions emitted in typed WebSocket events.
Event journal is durable, bounded and cursor-scoped; replay rechecks current access and returns explicit resync when cursor expires. Never claim cross-DO snapshot atomicity without protocol evidence.
Network administration does not grant access to private conversations. Explicit private metadata is owner-only across projection, GET/SUB/SYNC and replay.
Audit disabled means no records written. Enabled logs have actor/action/target/outcome/transport/time, no bearer/password/key/private message payload.
New sessions/cookies/scoped integration credentials preserve existing bearer defaults. Cookie mutations require session-bound CSRF token and exact allowed Origin.
Same-channel bulk operations are atomic where possible; multi-resource results disclose per-item outcomes and never imply a distributed transaction.
Durable event IDs plus client operation IDs prevent repeat mutations; read-only replay never applies a mutation.
New APIs document millisecond timestamps or ISO8601 explicitly, typed payloads/errors, operation IDs and bounds.
Account/channel generations fence retired identity and stale media/role grants. Re-registration creates fresh generation and cannot adopt old membership/media.
ChannelDO address remains networkId:canonicalName; resource_id generation fences archive/re-register callbacks. Old retained history moves to generation-keyed archive, inaccessible through new room.
REST membership uses internally generated api:<account UUID> provenance; real IRC session membership remains distinct; Session rechecks authoritative generation before reconciling.
Accounts must support both bearer/scoped-credential and verified accountId/credentialVersion operation authorization for IRC parity.
private: metadata is explicitly owner-only; existing ordinary custom IRC metadata remains public.
